subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can derivatives be used to describe change, curve behaviour, approximation and optimal values?

known_pitfalls.correction: A negative derivative indicates decrease with respect to the chosen variable.

known_pitfalls.claim: f prime(x)=0 always gives a maximum or minimum.
known_pitfalls.correction: A stationary point must be tested; it may be neither.

known_pitfalls.claim: The slope of the normal is always -f prime(x).
known_pitfalls.correction: When the tangent slope is nonzero, the normal slope is -1/f prime(x).

known_pitfalls.claim: The second derivative test works when f double prime(c)=0.
known_pitfalls.correction: If the second derivative is zero, the test is inconclusive.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 3 for the rate of increase of a circular wave area.
Use NCERT Example 10 to find increasing and decreasing intervals.
Use a Section 6.4 example to form tangent and normal equations.
Use a Section 6.5 example to approximate a nearby square root or power.
Use a Section 6.6 optimisation example and verify the extremum.
